newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Port project swells foreign investment in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Port project swells foreign investment in Vietnam.

text.p: Government approval for a deep-sea port project in southern Vietnam has reversed an apparent downturn in foreign investment, official media reports said on Tuesday.

The Vietnam News Agency (VNA) said a licence was granted last month for the $637-million Sao Mai-Ben Dinh port, a venture grouping Vietnam Maritime Corp, Taiwan's Evergreen Group, Malaysia Mining Corp and Singapore's Tredia Resources.
It said foreign-invested projects worth $920 million were licensed in October, taking the total approved since Hanoi launched economic reforms in the late 1980s to $24.7 billion.

Planning and Investment Minister Nguyen Xuan Gia told reporters on Monday that the value of projects licensed since January now stood at $5.0 billion, a little more than in the same period of last year.
Ministry of Planning and Investment figures had in recent months shown a decline of around 30 to 40 percent in approvals compared with corresponding periods a year earlier.
But the government has predicted that foreign investment this year will at least match 1995's record $7.4 billion.
The National Assembly last week approved a new law on foreign investment, incorporating amendments aimed at improving the business environment for non-Vietnamese firms.
Of all projects with foreign investment that have been approved over the past decade, only 30 percent have been implemented.
Investors and bankers blame red tape and an inadequate legal and regulatory framework -- both issues addressed by the new legislation -- for the pace of implementation.

VNA said the Sao Mai-Ben Dinh port, a build-operate-transfer (BOT) project, would accomodate cargo ships of up to 100,000 tonnes and oil tankers of up to 200,000 tonnes and have an annual handling capacity of 45 million tonnes a year by 2010.

The Marine Transport Department recently submitted plans to the government for a $5-billion nationwide port and shipping upgrade. The proposal aims to increase annual port handling capacity to 70 million tonnes by 2000 and 190 million tonnes by 2010, compared with 40 million today.
